title: Weak Chow lemma for a separated finite-type algebraic space over an affine scheme
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Give spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For morphisms of spaces, separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Locally of finite type and locally of finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed, where universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (agreeing with the scheme convention [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a separated finite-type morphism from an algebraic space. There exist an integer $n\ge0$, a quasi-compact separated scheme $X'$, a proper morphism $\pi:X'\to X$, and a quasi-compact immersion $j:X'\to\mathbf P^n_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ such that $a\pi=qj$, where $q$ is the projective-space projection [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. An immersion is a closed immersion into an open subscheme followed by its open inclusion [def-weil-open-immersion]. The map $\pi$ is universally surjective: for every algebraic space $W\to X$, the projection $X'\times_XW\to W$ is surjective on underlying point sets.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow); H-quasi-projectivity is the quasi-compact immersion in morphisms.tex Tag 01VW (definition-quasi-projective), (2). Universal surjectivity uses spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MH (lemma-base-change-surjective).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas], choose a representable surjective etale map $f:W\to X$ with $W$ affine. Quasi-compactness of $X$ follows from finite type over the affine base. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-maximum-degree] to see that $W$ is of finite type over $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and that the geometric fibre cardinalities are bounded. We prove the assertion, more generally for every such $X$ equipped with such an atlas whose fibres have cardinality at most $b$, by strong induction on $b$. For $b=0$, surjectivity forces $X$ empty; use $X'=\varnothing$ and its empty closed immersion into $\mathbf P^0_B$. For nonempty $X$, the cited node gives a least positive bound $d\leq b$, the nonempty maximum-degree open $U$, and an affine etale atlas $W_T\to T$ of the reduced closed complement with bound $d-1<b$.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), first paragraph; explicit induction statement and empty base case

proof.text: By [lem-chow-affine-immersion], embed $W$ into $\mathbf P^m_B$ through its closed immersion into the standard affine chart. This immersion is quasi-compact: the first map is closed and the standard chart is quasi-compact over the separated projective space. Apply [lem-chow-closed-model] to obtain its schematic closure $Y$, with $W\hookrightarrow Y$ open and $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_B$ closed. Now apply [lem-sfb-space-chow-configuration] to the atlas, $d$, $U$ and this compactification. Write its output as $V\subset H\subset Z$, $g_i:Z\to Y$, and $p:H\to X$. In particular $p$ is separated of finite type, $V\hookrightarrow H$ is quasi-compact and dense, the $g_i$ are proper, $H$ has the required quasi-compact projective-space immersion, and $p(V)=U$.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), configuration and compactification, through the properness claim

proof.text: Take a valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$, a map $v:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$, and $x:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ extending $p v$. The pullback $W_R=W\times_X\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a scheme, etale and surjective over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. In particular it is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Its image contains the closed point, so [lem-a1-flat-valuation-lifting] supplies an injective local extension of valuation rings $R\to R'$ and a lift $w:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to W$ of $x$. Put $K'=\operatorname{Frac}R'$. By the coordinate completeness in [lem-sfb-space-chow-configuration], the restriction of $w$ to $K'$ is one of the $d$ coordinates of $v_{K'}$, say the $i$th. This uses the whole split fibre, so no assumption that a mere pointwise representative descends to $K$ is made.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), valuation lifting through the etale atlas, including coordinate completeness

proof.text: Use $v_{K'}:\operatorname{Spec}K'\to V\subset Z$ and $w:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to W\subset Y$ as a valuation square for the proper scheme map $g_i:Z\to Y$. It commutes by the choice of $i$. By [lemma-nagata-proper-valuative-criterion-existence-api] there is a lift $z:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to Z$ with $g_i z=w$. Since $w$ factors through $W$, the universal property of the open inverse image makes $z$ factor through $g_i^{-1}(W)\subset H$. On that open, $p=f g_i$, so $p z=f w=x_{R'}$. Its generic restriction is the original $v_{K'}$. Thus every diagram required by [lem-sfb-space-dense-open-valuative-proper] has an extension after an injective local valuation-ring extension. To check its corrected affine-test quasi-compactness, use [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. The configuration gives quasi-compact $H$ and $V$ ($V$ is clopen in the affine $F$). Its separated scheme $H$ is quasi-separated. Also $X$ is absolutely quasi-separated: $X\to B$ is separated, $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and on each affine test the absolute diagonal factors as the closed relative diagonal followed by the pullback of the closed diagonal of $B$; hence it is a closed immersion and quasi-compact. The cited permanence node now makes $p:H\to X$ and $h:V\to H$ quasi-compact on affine tests. Local finite type and separatedness of $p$, and density of $h$, are supplied by [lem-sfb-space-chow-configuration]. It follows that $p$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), proof of the properness claim, final valuation square

proof.text: Let $i:T\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced closed subspace with support $|X|\setminus U$ from [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its map to $X$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper]. The composite $T\to B$ is separated and of finite type: on scheme charts its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $X\to B$, and its affine coordinate algebras are quotients of finite-type $A$-algebras. It is quasi-compact since $|T|$ is closed in the quasi-compact $|X|$. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-maximum-degree], $W_T\to T$ is a surjective etale atlas from an affine scheme with fibres bounded by $d-1<b$. The induction hypothesis therefore gives a proper surjection $T'\to T$ from a quasi-compact separated scheme with a quasi-compact immersion into a finite $B$-projective space. Its composite $T'\to X$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition].

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), induction on d and the reduced closed complement

proof.text: Set $X'=H\amalg T'$ and let $\pi:X'\to X$ restrict to the two maps just obtained. Both are proper. The finite disjoint union map is proper directly on tests: it is separated because its diagonal is the disjoint union of the two closed diagonals in the matching components, with empty inverse images in the cross components; it is of finite type by the two finite-type open pieces and their finite union; after every base change the image of a closed subset is the union of its two closed images. The source is quasi-compact and separated for the same finite-component reasons. The image of $H$ contains $U$, since $p(V)=U$, and the image of $T'$ contains $|X|\setminus U$. Thus $\pi$ is surjective. This completes the inductive construction.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), proper surjectivity of the final disjoint union

proof.text: To combine the two projective-space immersions, put their ambient projective spaces $\mathbf P^r_B$ and $\mathbf P^s_B$ into complementary coordinate linear subspaces of $\mathbf P^{r+s+1}_B$. These closed subspaces are disjoint: a point in their intersection would have every homogeneous coordinate zero. Their union is closed, and its induced scheme is their disjoint union, as the two defining homogeneous ideals sum to the irrelevant ideal. The two quasi-compact immersions give a quasi-compact immersion of $H\amalg T'$ into this disjoint union, and then into $\mathbf P^{r+s+1}_B$: factor each immersion through an open in its component and take the union of those opens. The resulting $j$ is over $B$, hence $a\pi=qj$. This also covers an empty component by omitting it.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), H-quasi-projectivity of the finite disjoint union, homogeneous-coordinate expansion

proof.text: Finally let $Q\to X$ be any algebraic space and $q\in|Q|$. Choose a point $x'\in|X'|$ over the image of $q$ using surjectivity. By the field-valued point equivalence in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], representatives of $q$ and $x'$ have extensions to a common field on which their maps to $X$ agree. The resulting pair is a point of $X'\times_XQ$ mapping to $q$. Thus every such projection is surjective, as required. This is the point-class proof of Tag 03MH; it uses no representability assumption on $Q\to X$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), with the induction and the universal-surjectivity argument made explicit.
